p: The matter of the rejoicing of this day
of "And you shall rejoice in your festival" (Devarim 16:14),
כְּעִנְיַן אָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים סח, ב)
in the manner of what our Sages of blessed memory said (Pesachim 68b):
because of the giving of the Torah."
that the day of the giving of the Torah
Was not the essential giving of the Tablets,
and in the Mishnah at the end of Taanis (Taanis 26b)
the day of the giving of the Torah,
and all the more so on the festival of Shavuos,
when the Torah had not yet been given,
only they heard from the mouth of the Almighty
However, the root of the matter
is from Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
about whom it is said (Melachim I 3:15),
"And he made a feast for all his servants,"
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, א, ט)
and our Sages of blessed memory said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1:9):
"From here we learn that one makes a meal
at the completion of the Torah."
And from this they also learned
that on Atzeres we require "for you."
As is known, all the mitzvos of the entire Torah
are called "the six hundred thirteen counsels"
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פב, ב),
meaning that it gives a person counsel
how there should become fixed in his heart
And this is the intent of the entire Torah,
to instruct and to teach a person
namely His Providence, may He be blessed, over everything.
And this is the essence of the completion of the Torah
that took place on the festival of Shavuos,
as our Sages of blessed memory said
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ב, ד, עַל הַפָּסוּק יִשָּׁקֵנִי)
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2:4, on the verse "Let him kiss me"):
"At the time that the Holy One, blessed be He, said
words of Torah became fixed in their hearts."
אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סא, א)
our Sages of blessed memory said (Bereishis Rabbah 61:1)
about Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared for him
and they would teach him Torah.
And seemingly, what do the kidneys have to do
וּבְלֵב כָּל חֲכַם לֵב נָתַתִּי חָכְמָה,
"And in the heart of every wise-hearted one I have placed wisdom,"
which is the dwelling place of wisdom?
of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him:
to reach the level of "I am,"
that is, to the truth of His Providence, may He be blessed,
that there is no palace without a master;
and to this one comes specifically
through the six hundred thirteen counsels.
And from where did he learn this,
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him?
About this our Sages of blessed memory said
that He prepared for him his two kidneys,
and they gave him counsel and sound wisdom
to reach the goal of his quest
even before the giving of the Torah.
And this is what was said
לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (שְׁמוֹת ו, ג)
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him (Shemos 6:3):
"but by My Name Hashem I did not make Myself known to them";
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעוֹד לֹא נִיתְּנָה לָהֶם הַתּוֹרָה
meaning that the Torah had not yet been given to them,
which is the making known of His Name, may He be blessed,
is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He,"
just as one calls a person by his name
לְהַכִּיר עַל יְדֵי זֶה אֶת עַצְמוּתוֹ.
to recognize through it his very essence.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן עַל יְדֵי קְרִיאַת הַתּוֹרָה
And likewise, through the reading of the Torah
one comes to the truth of His Providence, may He be blessed.
And as our Sages of blessed memory said (Berachos 21a):
"From where do we derive the blessing over the Torah?
'When I call out the Name of Hashem,
is the calling out of His Name, may He be blessed.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ו, א)
And so our Sages of blessed memory said (Berachos 6a)
that an individual who engages in Torah,
the Holy One, blessed be He, blesses him,
where I cause My Name to be mentioned";
and that is through the Torah.
And it is known that the Name Havayah, blessed be He,
of His Providence, may He be blessed,
which brings all the worlds into being,
and the other Names and appellations
And this is "but by My Name Hashem
I did not make Myself known to them":
that the essential level of knowing and recognizing
the Name Havayah, blessed be He,
וְלָזֶה זָכָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, merited
of Havayah, blessed be He, in completeness,
because the Torah was given through him.
And this is the essence of the completion of the Torah,
in accordance with our words above.
And about this our Sages of blessed memory said
also regarding Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
that one makes a meal at the completion of the Torah;
כִּי גַּם שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him, too
of the wisdom of His Providence, may He be blessed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם (מְלָכִים א ג, טו)
as it is said there (Melachim I 3:15):
"And Shlomo awoke, and behold, it was a dream" —
and he knows what it is chirping, and so on.
is the time of the rejoicing of the Torah,
the aspect of the completion of the Torah,
that it is the time of "the wellspring of the Torah,"
to be absorbed and held back
within the inner point of the heart:
the truth of His Providence, may He be blessed;
that is, that the words of Torah became fixed
in the heart, as mentioned above.
And for this reason it is customary to drink
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
as it is said of Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
with the expression "And he made a feast" — mishteh,
and a feast is called mishteh
only on account of the wine.
where the expression mishteh is mentioned
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁתֵּה הַיַּיִן.
is that it be specifically through the drinking of wine.
as it is said regarding Yosef (Bereishis 43:31):
for this was his main intent:
for the sanctity of the Shabbos meal,
only through this it came about
"and they drank and became intoxicated with him" (ibid. 43:34),
for this was his main intent:
and from this it came about afterward
that he drank from the vessels of the Beis HaMikdash
where only the expression mishteh is mentioned,
it is only because this was
the ultimate intent of the whole Megillah,
for through this Vashti was killed:
"When the heart of the king was merry with wine,
words of contempt because he had become drunk,
and this was the main cause
of the sprouting of the salvation:
And the essential root of the aspect of mishteh
is alluded to in the holy Torah (Bereishis 21:8):
on the day Yitzchak was weaned,"
וְדָרְשׁוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים קיט, ב) עַל זֶה
and our Sages of blessed memory expounded on it (Pesachim 119b)
that in the future the Holy One, blessed be He,
will make a feast for the tzaddikim
on the day He bestows His kindness
And this is the ultimate rectification and clarification
as our Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin 99a)
that they will drink the wine preserved in its grapes
since the six days of Creation.
And this is the rectification of the blemish
of the six days of Creation,
which came about because she squeezed grapes
and gave it to him, as is known.
And also according to the plain meaning
of "And Avraham made a great feast
on the day Yitzchak was weaned,"
that it is on the eighth day after his birth —
"he-gimmel mal," on the eighth he was circumcised —
to the root of the rectification of the first corruption,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מַאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח, ב)
as is known from the statement of our Sages of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 38b)
that is, at the time that he was created —
עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט) —
and only after the blemish of the sin
and through this all his descendants
with the covering of the foreskin
that is drawn from the cause of the first blemish.
וְהַגַּם שֶׁגַּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And although Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, too
at the command of Hashem, may He be blessed,
there was not yet in this
the complete rectification of the blemish for the community,
for it was only he himself
who circumcised himself with his own understanding.
אָמְנָם בְּמִילַת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
However, with the circumcision of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
who was the first to be circumcised at eight days,
through this a rectification was made
for the entire community of Yisrael
who are circumcised at eight days:
גַּם בְּעֵת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דַּעַת מֵעַצְמוֹ,
even when he has no understanding of his own,
the holiness is rooted in him through this,
so that he will be called
even if he corrupts his deeds
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א צג, א),
as is found in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 93a);
"Konam, that I will not benefit from the uncircumcised," etc.,
וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִלָּה יז, ב)
And to this our Sages of blessed memory alluded (Megillah 17b):
why did they establish the blessing of healing as the eighth?
Because circumcision was given on the eighth day,
And this is because the root of circumcision on the eighth day
indicates the ultimate healing and rectification
וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה י, ד)
and as our Sages of blessed memory said (Bereishis Rabbah 10:4)
עַל מַחַץ מַכָּתוֹ יִרְפָּא (יְשַׁעְיָה ל, כו)
on "and the wound of His blow He will heal" (Yeshayahu 30:26):
"the wound of the blow of the world He will heal."
which is the ultimate clarification and rectification
through the drinking of the wine
since the six days of Creation,
which will be in the time to come,
בְּיוֹם חֲבוֹשׁ ה׳ אֶת שֶׁבֶר עַמּוֹ
"on the day Hashem binds up the breach of His people,"
and the wound of the blow of the world He will heal.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן לְעֵת עַתָּה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And likewise, for now, in this world,
of the aspect of the rectification,
in the matter of circumcision at eight days
or in the matter of the completion of the Torah,
the aspect of the drinking of wine,
